name: Huawei Ascend 910D
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: THIS RECORD IS DELIBERATELY ALMOST EMPTY, and that is the honest finding rather than a gap in the research. 910D is a part I can substantiate EXISTENCE for but not SHIPPING, and the distinction matters: the only traceable public reporting is a WSJ story carried in cn-hisilicon-wikipedia stating that in late April 2025 Huawei approached several China-based companies to begin TESTING 910D, with first samples expected in May 2025. Sampling to a handful of integrators is not volume shipment. No specification of any kind has been published by Huawei, no compute figure, no memory figure, no die size, no process node, and no independent teardown exists - unlike the 910B, which at least drew SemiAnalysis and TechInsights attention. Every field above is None because every field is unknown, and inventing a plausible number here would be the exact failure mode this record exists to prevent. What can be said with evidence: 910D occupies the slot immediately after 910C and before the announced Ascend 920 (SMIC 6 nm, HBM3 at 4 TB/s, 900 TFLOPs per card, announced April 2025 for late-2025 production - and note even the 920's figures are announcement claims with no shipped product behind them as of the access date). If 910D is sampling and the 920 is announced, the plausible read is that 910D is a 7 nm N+2-family refinement sold into 2025 while the 920 is the 6 nm jump. Treat this record as an open question, revisit if Huawei publishes or a teardown appears.
